body.statement: The program defining \(V_c\) is feasible and attains its value for every \(\xi\in\mathbb R^{S_c}\). It is finite, even, convex, continuous, and positively homogeneous, with dual representation \[V_c(\xi)=\max\{\ell^\top \xi:|\ell^\top b_t|\le\theta_t^2\text{ for every }t\in\mathcal T_c\}.\] Moreover, \(0<\min_{t:\theta_t\ne0}|\theta_t|\le\kappa(c)\le1\), and the selected score obeys \((g^\star)^\top v=1\), \((g^\star)^\top\mathbf1=0\), and \(|(g^\star)^\top b_t|\le\theta_t^2/\kappa(c)\) for all \(t\).
body.justification: This finite-alphabet gauge is the first named multiarm object and its dual is directly observable from assignment labels.
body.gap: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen reduce the two-arm game to a scalar binomial experiment; their Theorems 2.1--2.3 contain no \(2^J\)-type gauge or full-label dual score.
body.consumer: The dual inequalities supply the uniform variance-pressure bound needed by both the attaining estimator and the tube-prior converse.
